column1: # parser/spec/lex.tsv — the trivia-preserving lexer parity corpus.
# Exactly three tab-separated columns: escaped source, OK/ERR clean-EOF
# status, and the exact token stream as canonical JSON. Token `si` values are
# UTF-8 byte offsets. Every column uses the parser/spec escape notation.
# Both ports own independent strict readers and renderers; keep the exact
# row-count ratchets in those runners and parser/spec/README.md in sync.
# Adjacent string quotes are unconditional #TX boundaries, including after
# the slash that follows a completed receiver.
# § base-prefixed boundaries — the class the decimal-boundary matcher's
#   base-prefix arm exists for. WITHOUT that arm the two stock scanners
#   disagree here (this is the gap that let the arm look retirable once):
#   before a `.`, Go's stock scanner calls `0xFF` a number and this port's
#   calls it text. These rows pin the token classification so a retirement
#   sweep must measure it instead of trusting the suites' silence.
#   READ THIS BEFORE USING THESE ROWS AS EVIDENCE. The stock scanners only
#   disagree for SOME follow characters: TS decides the run before the dot
#   by looking PAST the dot, so `0xFF.5` and `0xFF.e5` diverge without the
#   arm while `0xFF.x` agrees. Probing an agreeing shape and concluding the
#   arm is dead is precisely the mistake this section exists to prevent, so
#   one of each is pinned and labelled.
